twoFactor.intro: With two-factor sign-in on, you'll be asked for a six-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.) in addition to your password. You'll also get eight single-use recovery codes for when you can't reach the app.
twoFactor.enabledIntro: Signing in to this account requires a code from your authenticator app in addition to your password.
twoFactor.noCodesLeft: All recovery codes have been used; if you lose access to the app, the account can only be recovered through support.
twoFactor.setupIntro: Enter this secret in your authenticator app or scan/add its URI, then enter the current six-digit code to confirm:
twoFactor.uriLabel: otpauth URI to add to your app
twoFactor.recoveryTitle: These codes are shown only this once
twoFactor.recoveryDesc: Each code works only once, and you can't view them again after closing this section. Store them somewhere safe — each one is accepted once at sign-in in place of an app code.
twoFactor.disableIntro: To turn it off, you need your current password and a valid code (from the app or a recovery code):

guarantee.title: What does this page guarantee?
guarantee.body: Signing out a device revokes its session on the server; even if that device's token was copied earlier, it's no longer accepted. Each device's "last activity" is recorded from that session's real traffic. If you don't recognize a device, sign it out and, for extra security, use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page to set a new password for your account.
